question.text: Merkel belongs to this German political party, which is mainly opposed by the Social Democratic Party.
question.clue: This party's leaders Ludwig Erhard and Konrad Adenauer sparked an "economic miracle" in its country post-World War II, and it has participated in various "Grand Coalitions" with the Social Democratic Party.

swap.leadin: In order to crack this German code, Polish and British cryptographers designed mechanical devices called "bombes" [bombs].
swap.text: Name this supposedly unbreakable code that was finally cracked by codebreakers at Bletchley Park.
swap.clue: This device was combated by the bombe, a form of early computer.

question.leadin: Name these high ranking Nazi officials.
question.text: This head of the German Navy became leader of the Third Reich following Hitler's suicide and ordered the German surrender that ended World War II in Europe.
question.clue: Following Hitler's suicide, this admiral served for nearly a month as president of Germany in a government with Chancellor Goebbels ].

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Operation Overlord.
swap.text: This German general, known as the Desert Fox, was partially in charge of the defense of Normandy. Prior to his service in France, he fought in North Africa with the Afrikakorps.
swap.clue: This commander of the Ghost Division, victor at Kasserine Pass, and supporter of the Black Orchestra was arrested in connection with the 20th of July Plot, after which he committed suicide.

question.leadin: Name these political entities that heavily relied on maritime trade.
question.text: This confederation of German towns and merchants dominated the Baltic Sea trade. After defeating Waldemar IV's forces, this federation received a veto over successors to the Danish throne.
question.clue: Ivan III closed this polity's Kontor at Novgorod, and this organization achieved its peak when it formed the Confederation of Cologne.

swap.text: Along with Erich Ludendorff, Hitler earlier had tried to lead this failed 1923 uprising in Munich. It ended with his arrest, and while in jail, he published Mein Kampf.
swap.clue: In the aftermath of this event, Georg Neithardt sentenced its main perpetrator to only 8 months in prison after being impressed by his oratory skills, which led to Erich Ludendorff's acquittal.

question.leadin: Helmuth von Moltke remarked that although "in its original form [this document] sounded like a parley," now, it was like a "flourish of trumpets in answer to a challenge."
question.text: Name this document edited by Otto von Bismarck, which prompted a neighboring country to declare war on Prussia.
question.clue: During this event, "aide-de-camp" was rendered as "non-commissioned officer", an insult to Count Benedetti, who had been told by the Duke of Gramont to ask about the candidate chosen by Juan Prim for the Spanish throne.

swap.text: One of Bismarck's biggest blunders was the implementation of this campaign against Catholic influence. Many Catholics joined the Centre party as a result of it.
swap.clue: This social conflict came to an end with the passage of the First Mitigation Law negotiated following the death of Pius IX ], allowing clerics to be exempt from some Prussian laws.

question.leadin: This man won the 1926 Nobel Prize with Aristide Briand and had earlier negotiated the Dawes Plan.
question.text: Name this Foreign Minister who signed the Locarno Treaties to remove foreign occupation of the Rhineland and signed the Treaty of Berlin with Soviet Union.
question.clue: This man's 102-day tenure in that highest post ended after continuous harassment from Hans von Seeckt, but he was able to replace the Papiermark and issue the Rentenmark while in that office.

swap.leadin: Name these other medieval groups of knights.
swap.text: Founded in 1190 by German soldiers in the Third Crusade, they were charged with converting the pagans of eastern Europe but ended up taking political control of the region.
swap.clue: It was headquartered in Marienburg for the most successful part of its history, and was notably defeated at Lake Peipus by Alexander Nevsky.

question.leadin: This man built on the methods of the Gottingen School in his 1829 book on the First Serbian Uprising, which directly analyzed accounts provided by the philologist Vuk Karadzic ("KAH-ruh-jitch").
question.text: Name this prolific German historiographer. This spurner of a teleological theory of history attempted to elucidate the shared experiences between various European nations in his History of the Latin and Teutonic Peoples.
question.clue: While opposing Carr's relativism, Elton defended the more traditional, "scientific" methods used by this German historian. This historian classified European peoples into "Teutonic" and "Latin" groups in an 1824 book.

swap.leadin: This document begins by stating that "When our Lord and Master Jesus Christ said, 'Repent,' he willed the entire life of believers to be one of repentance"
swap.text: Name this 1517 document written by an Augustinian friar. This document was likely first sent in a letter to Archbishop Albert of Mainz and was legendarily nailed to a church door in Wittenberg.
swap.answerHtml: The 95 Theses [or Disputation on the Power and Efficacy of Indulgences; prompt on, but DO NOT REVEAL, Martin Luther’s Theses]
swap.clue: Konrad Wimpina defended the Dominican priest that was the main target of this work by writing a defense whose title puns on it.

question.text: Barnstormers often performed in groups called Flying Circuses. This nobleman led a fighter pilot squadron in World War I nicknamed the Flying Circus.
question.answerHtml: Manfred von Richthofen [or Manfred Albrecht Freiherr von Richthofen; or the Red Baron]
question.clue: His 80 kills led all aces during war, though he did not survive it; his famed red Fokker triplane was downed in April 1918, with both Australian anti-aircraft gunners and Canadian pilot Roy Brown claiming credit.

swap.text: The Germans achieved success near the end of the War by using these troops to break the trench stalemate. Oskar von Hutier pioneered their tactics, which were used to great success during the Ludendorff Offensive.
swap.answerHtml: stormtroopers [or stoßtruppen; sturmmann; sturmtruppen; prompt on translations like shock troops or assault troops]
swap.clue: German victory at Caporetto was partially due to the use of these soldiers. These units used "infiltration tactics" to overwhelm enemy trenches, and their name in German roughly translates as "shock troops."

question.text: A royal opponent of the 1832 Reform Bill was this uncle of Queen Victoria who served as Duke of Clarence and became the first person since George I to be the ruler of Hanover but not the ruler of Britain.
question.answerHtml: Ernest Augustus I of Hanover [or Duke of Clarence before mention; prompt on “Ernest Augustus”]

swap.leadin: According to Einhard, 4,500 of these people were executed in a single day at Verden.
swap.text: Name these people, who were defeated at the battle of Bornhoved ("born-HER-vet") during an invasion of their homeland that began in 772.
swap.answerHtml: Saxons [accept Nordalbingian Saxons; do not accept or prompt on “Anglo-Saxons”]
swap.clue: These people were protected by forts called burhs during the Heptarchy.

question.leadin: After this man was able to escape the grasps of Frederick I of Prussia, who was trying to learn of alchemy, he was caught by Augustus the Strong.
question.text: Name this man who, in collaboration with the scientist Ehrenfried von Tschirnhaus in the pursuit of alchemy, accidentally brought porcelain-making to Europe at the Meissen factory.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Adolf Hitler and birthdays.
swap.text: This Nazi Minister of Propaganda held lavish festivities in Berlin in honor of Hitler's fiftieth birthday. This man gave the "Total War" speech in 1943.
swap.clue: The Sportpalast speech was given by this man, who stated that "Germany ... has no intention of bowing to this Jewish threat."

question.leadin: Willibald claimed that Saint Boniface took this inflammatory action before constructing a church dedicated to Saint Peter.
question.text: Describe this symbolic action done to end a decades-long conflict to forcibly christianize a people who lived northeast of Austrasia under their leader Widukind.
question.answerHtml: chopping down a sacred tree [accept answers like chopping down the Irminsul, cutting down Donar’s Oak, or removing a stump; prompt on chopping down, cutting, removing, or similar answers by asking “to what object”]

swap.leadin: Goethe's dramatic rendition of his life has him say the phrase "Kiss my ass" when he told it to the Bishop of Bamberg.
swap.text: Identify this German hero and mercenary that is known for fighting in the Peasants War against the Holy Roman Emperor. He had a prosthetic hand.
swap.clue: This play about an iron-armed soldier whose nemesis Weislingen has him arrested. Weislingen is eventually poisoned on the orders of the beautiful Adelheid.
